tagline: From Bogalusa's mill town over the Mississippi to the Red River.
intro: The parkway runs 203 miles from Bogalusa west to Pineville, by Franklinton, Clinton and St. Francisville, over the Mississippi to New Roads and on through Marksville and Alexandria, crossing three other Louisiana byways as it goes. It is named for Zachary Taylor, who served in the War of 1812 and the Mexican-American War and made Baton Rouge his adopted home.

Bogalusa, at the east end, was built in the early 1900s as a company town for the Great Southern Lumber Company, whose sawmill was the largest in the world at the time. Its name comes from Choctaw words for dark or smoky water.

moments.title: Clinton
moments.text: The courthouse and Lawyer's Row, Greek Revival buildings, make up the heart of a National Historic Landmark district in a town that has been the parish seat since 1824.

moments.title: John James Audubon Bridge
moments.text: The only bridge across the Mississippi between Natchez and Baton Rouge opened in May 2011, ahead of schedule, because the rising river had shut down the ferry it was built to replace.

moments.title: Forts Randolph and Buhlow
moments.text: At Pineville the remains of Bailey's Dam recall how Admiral Porter's Union fleet got back down past the Red River rapids in the retreat after the Battle of Mansfield.
